newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: RINGGIT SLIPS TO 2.66/DLR AFTER MAHATHIR'S REMARKS.
newsitem.headline: RINGGIT SLIPS TO 2.66/DLR AFTER MAHATHIR'S REMARKS.

text.p: The ringgit fell 100 points to a 39-month low against the dollar late on Friday after Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad said he was happy with the level of ringgit, despite the local unit's sharp recent falls, dealers said.
At 1215 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.6605/55 to a dollar, its lowest level since May 5, 1994.
"There's big buying of dollar/Malay out of London. They are pushing the dollar higher," said a dealer with a U.S. bank in London. "The market is trying to pick stops."
Dealers said Mahathir's remark gave players a further excuse to buy up dollar/ringgit.
"We are happy with the current level of the ringgit," Mahathir told reporters. "The value (of ringgit) went down, but for us it does not matter."
He said the ringgit's fall of about five percent against the dollar was not much "if compared with the deutschemark which has fallen by 17 percent."
Dealers said dollar/ringgit could be heading for 2.70.
At 1240 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.6830/60 a dollar.
